questions.question_text: $\frac{3}{5}$ of a quantity is $18$. What is the whole?

options.why: This finds one fifth but stops before rebuilding the whole.
This multiplies by the denominator without first finding one part.

questions.question_text: Four of seven equal tape sections total $28$. What is the full tape value?

options.why: This finds one section but not all seven sections.
This multiplies 28 by 7 without dividing by four.

questions.question_text: $\frac{5}{8}$ of a tank is $40$ L. What is its capacity?

options.why: This gives the value of one eighth only.
This multiplies the known part by eight without dividing by five.

questions.question_text: If $\frac{2}{3}$ of a number is $14$, which calculation finds the number?

options.why: Applies the fraction forwards instead of reversing it, working out $\frac{2}{3}$ of $14$ rather than the whole.
Multiplies by the numerator and the denominator, never dividing by $2$ to find the value of one third first.

questions.question_text: A box is $\frac{7}{10}$ full with $42$ items. How many spaces are empty?

options.why: This finds one tenth but not the three empty tenths.
This gives the whole capacity rather than the empty spaces.
This finds the $18$ empty spaces, then subtracts them from the $42$ filled spaces as though $42$ were the whole capacity.

questions.question_text: $\frac{4}{9}$ of a quantity is $36$. A student answers $144$. What step is missing?

options.text: Multiply the one-part value by $9$, not the known value by $4$.

options.why: This calculates four ninths of 36 rather than reconstructing the whole.
Adding fraction numbers does not reverse the fractional part.
